summary.excess_detail: 5 of 10 attached Allow statements are wildcard/over-broad

findings.title: Full administrator access (Action "*" on Resource "*") via AWS managed policy AdministratorAccess
findings.description: The statement grants every action on every resource in the account. Holders can create users and keys, rewrite any policy, read all data, disable CloudTrail/GuardDuty and delete resources.
findings.attack_scenario: Credential theft of this identity = full account takeover. An attacker typically creates a backdoor user or access key (persistence), disables logging (defense evasion) and exfiltrates S3/RDS/Secrets data.
findings.recommendation: Remove standing admin. Use role-based, MFA-gated, time-bound elevation (IAM Identity Center permission set or an assumable break-glass role) and protect security tooling with explicit Deny.

findings.title: Administrator is a long-lived IAM user
findings.description: test-admin is an IAM user with full administrator rights. IAM users carry long-lived credentials (password / access keys).
findings.attack_scenario: Leaked access keys of an admin IAM user never expire; MFA cannot be enforced on API keys without explicit conditions.
findings.recommendation: Use IAM Identity Center or an assumable admin role with MFA and short sessions; remove the user's direct admin policy.

findings.title: Privilege escalation: PassRole to new Lambda function
findings.description: Can create a Lambda function that executes attacker code with any passable execution role. Required permissions present: iam:PassRole, lambda:CreateFunction.
findings.attack_scenario: 1) test-passrole calls lambda:CreateFunction with --role pointing at a privileged role/policy (allowed by iam:PassRole on that ARN). 2) The function code reads AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID/SECRET/SESSION_TOKEN from its environment or calls IAM directly. 3) Once invoked, the attacker operates with the execution role's privileges.
findings.recommendation: Scope iam:PassRole to the exact execution role ARN(s) and add Condition StringEquals iam:PassedToService = lambda.amazonaws.com; scope the compute action to a function/instance naming prefix.
notes: No role in this export currently trusts lambda.amazonaws.com; PassRole on "*" means the escalation becomes immediate the moment any privileged role trusting lambda.amazonaws.com exists (common for Lambda/EC2 execution roles).

No trigger permission (lambda:InvokeFunction / lambda:CreateEventSourceMapping / lambda:CreateFunctionUrlConfig / lambda:AddPermission) found - the chain is one permission away from executable, or relies on an existing event source / another principal to invoke it.

findings.title: Sensitive action(s) allowed on Resource "*" (Compute / code execution, Privilege escalation primitive)
findings.description: 2 sensitive action(s) apply to every resource: iam:PassRole, lambda:CreateFunction.
findings.attack_scenario: iam:PassRole on "*" lets the holder hand ANY role (including admin roles) to an AWS service it controls. Code-execution APIs on "*" allow running attacker-controlled code inside the account.
findings.recommendation: Scope Resource to the specific ARNs (bucket, function, parameter path, role) and add guardrail conditions (aws:ResourceAccount, iam:PassedToService, aws:MultiFactorAuthPresent).

findings.title: Service-wide wildcard s3:* on all resources
findings.description: s3:* grants every current and future API of the service, including 12 known-sensitive action(s) such as s3:DeleteBucket, s3:DeleteBucketPolicy, s3:DeleteObject, s3:DeleteObjectVersion, s3:GetObject, s3:GetObjectVersion.
findings.attack_scenario: The holder can read and download every object in every bucket (data exfiltration), make buckets public via s3:PutBucketPolicy / PutBucketAcl, and destroy data with s3:DeleteBucket / DeleteObject (ransomware pattern).
findings.recommendation: Replace the service wildcard with the specific read/write actions the workload needs and scope Resource to named ARNs.

findings.title: Recently created privileged user (created 1 day(s) ago)
findings.description: test-admin was created 2026-11-17 13:12 UTC and already holds high-risk permissions.
findings.attack_scenario: Creating a new privileged IAM user/role is a classic persistence technique after initial compromise (T1136.003). Confirm it maps to an approved change ticket.
findings.recommendation: Verify the creator in CloudTrail (CreateUser/CreateRole events) and the business justification.

findings.attack_scenario: Creating a new privileged IAM user/role is a classic persistence technique after initial compromise (T1136.003). Confirm it maps to an approved change ticket.

findings.title: Sensitive action(s) allowed on Resource "*" (Credential / secret access)
findings.description: 2 sensitive action(s) apply to every resource: ssm:GetParameter, ssm:GetParameters.
findings.attack_scenario: Every parameter/secret in the account is readable - including database passwords and API tokens of other apps.
findings.recommendation: Scope Resource to the specific ARNs (bucket, function, parameter path, role) and add guardrail conditions (aws:ResourceAccount, iam:PassedToService, aws:MultiFactorAuthPresent).
notes: AWS-managed policy: you cannot edit it - replace it with a scoped customer-managed copy (generated below).

findings.title: Sensitive action(s) allowed on Resource "*" (Credential / secret access, Sensitive data read)
findings.description: 5 sensitive action(s) apply to every resource: cloudformation:GetTemplate, eks:AccessKubernetesApi, logs:FilterLogEvents, logs:GetLogEvents, logs:StartQuery.
findings.attack_scenario: All CloudWatch log data is readable (logs often contain tokens, PII and request payloads). Kubernetes API access on every EKS cluster (subject to cluster access entries).
findings.recommendation: Scope Resource to the specific ARNs (bucket, function, parameter path, role) and add guardrail conditions (aws:ResourceAccount, iam:PassedToService, aws:MultiFactorAuthPresent).
notes: AWS-managed policy: you cannot edit it - replace it with a scoped customer-managed copy (generated below).

findings.title: Permissions granted through inline user policy
findings.description: test-passrole has inline policies: ci-deploy. Inline user policies are invisible in policy inventories, cannot be reused or versioned, and bypass group-based access reviews.
findings.attack_scenario: Attackers favour inline policies for persistence because they are easy to overlook.
findings.recommendation: Move permissions to a versioned customer-managed policy attached to a group or role.

findings.title: Permissions granted through inline user policy
findings.description: test-s3-all has inline policies: s3-all. Inline user policies are invisible in policy inventories, cannot be reused or versioned, and bypass group-based access reviews.
findings.attack_scenario: Attackers favour inline policies for persistence because they are easy to overlook.
findings.recommendation: Move permissions to a versioned customer-managed policy attached to a group or role.

findings.title: Very broad permission surface: 989 actions across 190 services on "*"
findings.description: A single statement grants 989 actions across 190 services on all resources (mostly read/list).
findings.attack_scenario: Broad read access enables full reconnaissance of the account (T1580) and reading of operational data such as logs and templates.
findings.recommendation: Confirm the identity really needs account-wide visibility; otherwise restrict to the services in use.
notes: AWS-managed policy: you cannot edit it - replace it with a scoped customer-managed copy (generated below).

findings.title: Usage telemetry absent - dormancy cannot be assessed for some identities
findings.description: The export has no PasswordLastUsed / credential report data for 3 user(s): test-admin, test-passrole, test-s3-all. get-account-authorization-details does not include user login or access-key activity.
findings.attack_scenario: Unused credentials cannot be distinguished from active ones without telemetry.
findings.recommendation: Run `python cli.py collect` (adds the IAM credential report) or merge `aws iam get-credential-report` output into the export under the key "CredentialReport".

findings.title: Role assumable by ANY AWS principal ("Principal": "*")
findings.description: The trust policy allows every IAM principal in every AWS account to call sts:AssumeRole on this role.
findings.attack_scenario: An attacker with any AWS account (free tier) runs `aws sts assume-role --role-arn arn:aws:iam::111122223333:role/public-debug-role` and receives this role's credentials.
findings.recommendation: Replace "*" with the specific trusted account/role ARNs and add aws:PrincipalOrgID.

findings.title: OIDC trust to token.actions.githubusercontent.com without subject (sub) condition
findings.description: Any identity issued by token.actions.githubusercontent.com can assume this role - e.g. ANY GitHub repository in the world for GitHub Actions.
findings.attack_scenario: An attacker creates their own repo/pipeline, requests an OIDC token for audience sts.amazonaws.com and calls AssumeRoleWithWebIdentity on arn:aws:iam::111122223333:role/github-actions-deploy.
findings.recommendation: Add StringLike token.actions.githubusercontent.com:sub restricted to your org/repo/branch and StringEquals token.actions.githubusercontent.com:aud = sts.amazonaws.com.

findings.description: Trust delegates to arn:aws:iam::111122223333:root; every user/role whose identity policy allows sts:AssumeRole on this role can become it.
findings.attack_scenario: Lateral movement hub: a broad `sts:AssumeRole` on "*" anywhere in the account becomes a path to this role.
findings.recommendation: Trust specific role ARNs instead of the account root, or add aws:PrincipalArn / aws:PrincipalTag conditions.

changes: AWS-managed policies cannot be edited: this is a customer-managed replacement for AdministratorAccess.
Admin access restricted to the approved region(s).
Explicit Deny protects CloudTrail, GuardDuty, Config, Security Hub and Access Analyzer from tampering.
Preferred end-state: delete standing admin; grant an assumable break-glass role / IAM Identity Center permission set.

residual: HIGH ADMIN-001: Full administrator access (Action "*" on Resource "*")

changes: iam:AddUserToGroup moved from Resource "*" to arn:aws:iam::111122223333:role/<ROLE_NAME> with aws:ResourceAccount guardrail.
ec2:RunInstances moved from Resource "*" to arn:aws:ec2:<REGION>:111122223333:instance/* with aws:ResourceAccount guardrail.
iam:PassRole scoped to one execution role and limited to iam:PassedToService = ec2.amazonaws.com.
AWS-managed policies cannot be edited: this is a customer-managed replacement for PowerUserAccess.
NotAction (iam:*, organizations:*, account:*) replaced by an explicit read-only baseline + an allow-list for required writes.
iam:CreateServiceLinkedRole moved from Resource "*" to arn:aws:iam::111122223333:role/<ROLE_NAME> with aws:ResourceAccount guardrail.
Wildcard principal "*" replaced with an explicit role ARN and pinned to your AWS Organization (aws:PrincipalOrgID).
OIDC trust pinned to audience sts.amazonaws.com and subject repo:<GITHUB_ORG>/<REPO>:ref:refs/heads/main.
Admin access now requires an MFA-authenticated session younger than 1 hour (blocks leaked access keys).
Explicit Deny protects CloudTrail, GuardDuty, Config, Security Hub and Access Analyzer from tampering.
Preferred end-state: delete standing admin; grant an assumable break-glass role / IAM Identity Center permission set.

residual: HIGH ADMIN-001: Full administrator access (Action "*" on Resource "*")

changes: lambda:InvokeFunction, lambda:GetFunction moved from Resource "*" to arn:aws:lambda:<REGION>:111122223333:function:debug-* with aws:ResourceAccount guardrail.
logs:FilterLogEvents moved from Resource "*" to arn:aws:logs:<REGION>:111122223333:log-group:<LOG_GROUP>:* with aws:ResourceAccount guardrail.
s3:GetObject moved from Resource "*" to arn:aws:s3:::<BUCKET_NAME>, arn:aws:s3:::<BUCKET_NAME>/* with aws:ResourceAccount guardrail.
secretsmanager:GetSecretValue moved from Resource "*" to arn:aws:secretsmanager:<REGION>:111122223333:secret:<APP_PREFIX>/* with aws:ResourceAccount guardrail.
Added sts:ExternalId = f3c01564-4bd6-5ac1-bc68-864af3e17e04 for arn:aws:iam::999988887777:root (share it with the third party out-of-band).
Account root of 999988887777 narrowed to a single vendor integration role.
